Author: Sanjay Kumar Singh
Bench: Sanjay Kumar Singh
High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 40470 of 2022
Applicant :- Monu Sharma

sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State Of U.P. And 3 Others
Counsel for Applicant :- Anil Kumar Srivastava,Harikesh

Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sanjay Kumar Singh,J.
Despite service of notice upon the informant/opposite party no. 2, no one put in appearance on her behalf.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant and learned Additional Government Advocate representing the State.

The instant bail application under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. has been filed on behalf of the applicant with a prayer to release him on bail in Case Crime No. 297 of 2022, under Sections 363, 366, 376,
504, 506 I.P.C. and Section 5/6 Protection Of Children from Sexual Offences Act and 3(2)(5)
S.C.S.T. Act, Police Station- Mauaima, District- Prayagraj, during the pendency of trial.

entities.text: Protection Of Children from Sexual Offences Act
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text:
As per the prosecution case in brief, informant who is the mother of victim has lodged an F.I.R. on 08.06.2022 with regard to an incident which took place on 07.06.2022 against the applicant- Monu Monu Sharma vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76717113/
1 Sharma and co-accused Om Prakash Sharma, Manju Devi, Shivam Hela and Sharad alleging inter-alia that on 07.06.2022 at about 12:30 O'clock, her minor daughter, aged about 17 years was enticed away by the applicant.

entities.text: Monu Monu Sharma vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The F.I.R. further alleges that her daughter while going with the applicant also took away her mother's gold mangulsutra and Rs. 15,000/- with her.
It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that on 19.06.2022, victim herself returned to her home.
Thereafter, her statement under Section 161 and 164 Cr.P.C. was recorded, but she has not supported the prosecution case.

Heavy reliance has been placed on the statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. of the victim, wherein, she has stated inter-alia that on 06.06.2022 at about 10 O'clock,
she was scolded and beaten by her mother, therefore, she made a phone call to the applicant and thereafter they met with eachother in a restaurant and they went to Company Garden.
Later on, she went to Delhi with the applicant and stayed there in an Ashram and physical relation was made between them.
She has also disclosed that she has travelled to Varanasi along with the applicant and stayed there at the house of a friend of the applicant, where also physical relation was made between them.
It is also pointed out that, though, as per the prosecution case, victim is aged about 17 years but as per her ossification test report, her age has been found between 16-18 years.
On the strength of the aforesaid facts, it is submitted that, it is not a case of rape but it is a case of consensual sex between the parties concerned.
Lastly, it is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that there is no chance of the applicant of fleeing away from the judicial process or tampering with the prosecution evidence.

The applicant is languishing in jail since 14.07.2022 and having no criminal history and in case he is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail and will cooperate in the early disposal of the case.
Per contra, learned A.G.A. for the State opposed the prayer for bail of the applicant but could not dispute the above factual aspect of the matter as argued on behalf of the applicant.
Having heard learned counsel for the parties and examined the matter in its entirety, I find that victim is near to major and she is capable to understand the things for which she was consenting.

The victim has not supported the prosecution case in her statement under Section 164 Cr.P.C. and she appears to be consenting party with the applicant, therefore, possibility of false implication of the applicant could not be ruled out.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case as well as keeping in view the nature of the offence, evidence, complicity of the accused and submissions of the learned counsel for the parties, I am of the view that the applicant has made out a fit case for bail.
Hence, the bail application is hereby allowed.

Let the applicant- Monu Sharma,be released on bail in the aforesaid case crime number on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned with the following conditions which are being imposed in the interest of justice:-
(i) That the applicant shall cooperate in the expeditious disposal of the trial and shall regularly attend the court unless inevitable.
Monu Sharma vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 20 January, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76717113/

entities.text: Monu Sharma vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2 (ii) That the applicant shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade him from disclosing such facts to the court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
(iii) That after his release, the applicant shall not involve in any criminal activity.
(iv) The identity, status and residential proof of sureties will be verified by court concerned before the release of the applicant on bail.
In case of breach of any of the conditions mentioned above, court concerned will be at liberty to cancel the bail of the applicant.
